rules.point: an chopail, abairt rangaithe (Is + ainmfhocal + é/í)
rules.text: To say what a person is, the copula Is comes first, then the noun, then the pronoun: Is dochtúir é, Is múinteoir í. The pronoun é or í matches the sex of the person named.

rules.point: an chopail, ceist agus freagra (An ... é? Is ea / Ní hea)
rules.text: A classification question is formed with An + noun + é/í? and is answered with Is ea or Ní hea, never with tá. A correction can be added with atá ann: Ní hea. Dochtúir atá ann. (In Ulster speech Is ea is often heard as 'Sea; pupils write Is ea.)

rules.point: an chopail, Cén tslí bheatha atá ag ...?
rules.text: A person's occupation is asked with Cad é an tslí bheatha atá ag X? or Cad é an obair atá aige/aici? and answered with a copula sentence: Is polaiteoir é. The standard Cén tslí bheatha / Cén obair is also understood.

rules.point: an chopail i gclásal indíreach (gur)
rules.text: After a verb of opinion such as sílim, ceapaim or measaim, the copula Is becomes gur: Sílim gur feirmeoir é. Sílim is the usual Ulster verb; ceapaim and measaim are also correct.

rules.point: an chopail leis an aidiacht, Nach ... an ... é?
rules.text: An adjective can be placed before the noun with the copula for emphasis: Nach deas an rothar é? The answer repeats only the copula and the adjective: Is deas.

rules.point: an chopail san aimsir chaite, Ba / B'
rules.text: In the past tense the copula is Ba, which lenites the adjective after it, and B' before a vowel: Ba chumasach an cainteoir é, B'uafásach an timpiste í. Adjectives beginning with l, n, r or sp do not change in writing: Ba leadránach, Ba spórtúil.

rules.point: inscne agus an forainm é/í
rules.text: With a feminine noun the pronoun at the end is í (aimsir, áit, ceist, fadhb, obair, timpiste); with a masculine noun it is é.

rules.point: Sin é / Sin í / Sin iad
rules.text: To point someone out, Sin is followed by é, í or iad and then the name: Sin í Niamh, Sin é Peadar, Sin iad na cailíní.

rules.point: is maith le, is breá le, is fuath le
rules.text: Liking and disliking are expressed with the copula and the preposition le: Is maith le Peadar peil, Is fuath le Séamas deoch leighis. With a pronoun, le combines into liom, leat, leis, léi, linn, libh, leo.

rules.point: freagra ar An maith leat ...?
rules.text: A question with An maith leat? is answered by repeating the copula: Is maith liom, Is aoibhinn liom, Is breá liom for a positive reply, or Ní maith liom, Is fuath liom, Is gráin liom for a negative one. The negative of Is is Ní.

rules.point: is fearr le, rogha idir dhá rud
rules.text: Preference uses is fearr le: Cé acu is fearr leat popcheol nó snagcheol? Is fearr liom popcheol. A preference within a category is asked with Cad é an + noun + is fearr leat? and answered Is fearr liom .... The standard Cén + noun + is fearr leat? is also understood.

rules.point: úinéireacht, Cé leis é? Is liomsa é
rules.text: Ownership is expressed with le and the emphatic pronoun: Cé leis an peann? Is liomsa é, Ní liomsa é, An leatsa é? With a name the indirect form is used after sílim or ceapaim: sílim gur le Pól é.

rules.point: náisiúntacht leis an chopail
rules.text: Nationality is a classification sentence of the same shape as occupation: Is Rúiseach é.

r1-chaite.title: An chéad réimniú: an aimsir chaite

rules.point: an aimsir chaite, an chéad réimniú: séimhiú ar an gconsan tosaigh
rules.text: To form the past tense of a first-conjugation verb beginning with a consonant, lenite the initial consonant of the root (the order form): Dún becomes Dhún sé, Cuir becomes Chuir sé, Múch becomes Mhúch sé.

rules.point: an aimsir chaite: briathra nach nglacann séimhiú (l, n, r, sc, sp, st)
rules.text: Verbs whose root begins with a letter or cluster that cannot take lenition keep the root unchanged in the past tense: Las sé an tine, Scuab sé an t-úrlár, Rith sé go dtí an líne.

rules.point: an aimsir chaite: ceist agus diúltach le Ar agus Níor
rules.text: The question is formed with Ar and the negative with Níor, both followed by lenition of the verb: Ar dhún tú? Níor dhún mé. Ar chuir sé? Níor chuir sé. The pronoun subject follows the verb.

rules.point: an aimsir chaite: an chéad phearsa iolra, foirm tháite -amar/-eamar
rules.text: In Ulster the first person plural of the past tense is the root (lenited or with d' as usual) followed by the pronoun muid: dhún muid, chuir muid, d'ól muid, d'úsáid muid, d'fhág muid. Question and negative follow the same pattern: Ar dhún muid? Níor dhún muid. The standard synthetic endings -amar and -eamar (dhúnamar, chuireamar) will be met in books and exam papers and should be recognised, but pupils write the muid form.

rules.point: an aimsir chaite: an saorbhriathar, -adh/-eadh
rules.text: The autonomous form adds -adh to a broad root and -eadh to a slender root, and it is never lenited, even after Ar and Níor: Dúnadh, Ar dúnadh? Níor dúnadh; Cuireadh, Ar cuireadh? Níor cuireadh.

rules.point: an aimsir chaite: briathra a thosaíonn ar ghuta, d' roimh an mbriathar
rules.text: A verb beginning with a vowel takes the prefix d' in the positive past: D'ól sé, D'amharc sé, D'íoc sé, D'úsáid sé, D'éist sé. After Ar and Níor the d' is dropped: Ar ól tú? Níor ól mé. The autonomous form has no d': Óladh, Ar óladh? Níor óladh; Úsáideadh, Níor úsáideadh.

rules.point: an aimsir chaite: briathra a thosaíonn ar 'f', d'fh
rules.text: A verb beginning with f is lenited and also takes d' in the positive past: D'fhág sé, D'fhan sé, D'fhill sé, D'fhéach sé. After Ar and Níor there is lenition but no d': Ar fhág tú? Níor fhág mé. The autonomous form is neither lenited nor given d': Fágadh, Ar fágadh? Níor fágadh. Note that for 'look at' Ulster normally says amharc ar (d'amharc sé), so féach appears here only to show the f pattern.

lessons.title: Briathra nach nglacann séimhiú
lessons.rule: A verb beginning with l, n, r, sc, sm, sp or st cannot take séimhiú, so in the past tense the root stays exactly as it is: las, rith, scuab, scríobh. This is true after Níor as well: Níor scuab sé. But s followed by a vowel, l, n or r does take h: sheas, shiúil, shnámh.
steps: Find the root of the verb in brackets: las.
Check the first letter: l cannot take h.
Leave the root as it is and put it first: Las Pádraig an scáileán ar a fhón.

lessons.hint: l, n, r, sc, sm, sp and st: no h. S + vowel, l, n or r: h (sheas, shnámh).

lessons.en: Questions with Ar, negatives with Níor
lessons.rule: To ask a question put Ar before the verb, and for a negative put Níor; both lenite a consonant, and a vowel or f verb loses its d': Ar ól tú? Ar fhan tú? If the answer uses mé, ask with tú; if it uses muid, ask with sibh.
steps: Start from the answer: D'fhág mé.
Drop the d' and put Ar in front, keeping the h: Ar fhág.
Change mé to tú and add the rest: Ar fhág tú an leabhar anseo?

lessons.rule: When nobody is named as doing the action, add -adh to a broad root (last vowel a, o or u) and do not lenite it: díol becomes díoladh.

r1-laithreach.title: An chéad réimniú: an aimsir láithreach

rules.point: an aimsir láithreach, an chéad réimniú, briathra leathana
rules.text: For a first-conjugation verb with a broad final consonant, the present tense is formed by adding -ann to the root, which is the same as the order form: dún gives dúnann sé, glan gives glanann sé, múch gives múchann sé.

rules.point: an aimsir láithreach, an chéad réimniú, briathra caola
rules.text: For a first-conjugation verb with a slender final consonant, -eann is added to the root: cuir gives cuireann sé, blais gives blaiseann sé, rith gives ritheann sé.

rules.point: an aimsir láithreach, foirmeacha táite (mé, muid)
rules.text: The first person singular has its own ending, -aim after a broad root and -im after a slender one (dúnaim, cuirim). In Ulster the first person plural uses the ordinary -ann/-eann ending followed by muid: dúnann muid, cuireann muid. All other persons take -ann/-eann followed by the pronoun (dúnann tú, sé, sí, sibh, siad).

rules.point: an aimsir láithreach, an cheist agus an diúltach
rules.text: A question is formed with An followed by eclipsis of the verb (An ndúnann tú? An gcuireann sé?). The negative is formed with Ní followed by lenition (Ní dhúnaim, Ní chuireann sé).

rules.point: an aimsir láithreach, an saorbhriathar
rules.text: The free (autonomous) form ends in -tar after a broad root and -tear after a slender root: dúntar, cuirtear. The question is An ndúntar? and the negative Ní dhúntar; the free form has no separate pronoun.

rules.point: an aimsir láithreach, briathra a thosaíonn ar ghuta
rules.text: A verb beginning with a vowel takes the same endings (ólann sé, ólaim, ólann muid, óltar) but shows no change after An or Ní because a vowel can be neither eclipsed nor lenited: An ólann tú? Ní ólaim. Longer slender roots such as úsáid and éist follow the same pattern: úsáideann sé, úsáidim, úsáideann muid, úsáidtear, éisteann sé.

rules.point: an aimsir láithreach, briathra a thosaíonn ar f
rules.text: A verb beginning with f is eclipsed to bhf after An (An bhfágann tú?) and lenited to fh after Ní (Ní fhágaim, Ní fhágtar); otherwise it follows the ordinary pattern: fágann sé, fágaim, fágann muid, fágtar.

rules.point: an aimsir láithreach, freagra gairid
rules.text: A present-tense question is answered by repeating the verb in the right person, positively or negatively, without yes or no: An ndúnann tú an doras? Dúnaim / Ní dhúnaim. An ndúnann sibh an doras? Dúnann muid / Ní dhúnann muid. An ndúntar? Dúntar / Ní dhúntar.

lessons.title: -ann agus -eann
lessons.rule: In the present tense, add -ann to a broad root (last vowel a, o or u) and -eann to a slender root (last vowel i or e), then put the subject: glan becomes glanann sí, cuir becomes cuireann sí. With muid use the same form: glanann muid.
steps: Find the root of the verb in brackets: glan.
The last vowel is a, so the root is broad: add -ann to get glanann.
Put the verb first, then the subject: Glanann sí a seomra leapa.

lessons.en: Questions with An, negatives with Ní
lessons.rule: For a question put An before the verb and eclipse it (An gcaitheann, An bhfágann); for a negative put Ní before it and lenite it (Ní chaitheann, Ní fhágann). l, m, n, r and s do not change after An, and l, n, r, sc, sm, sp and st do not change after Ní.

r1-fhaistineach.title: An chéad réimniú: an aimsir fháistineach

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, an chéad réimniú, briathra leathana
rules.text: To form the future of a broad first conjugation verb, add -faidh to the root: Dún gives Dúnfaidh sé an doras, Glan gives Glanfaidh sé an bord.

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, an chéad réimniú, briathra caola
rules.text: To form the future of a slender first conjugation verb, add -fidh to the root: Cuir gives Cuirfidh sé an pláta ar an bhord, Bain gives Bainfidh sé an féar. Note the Ulster lenition after ar an: ar an bhord, not ar an mbord.

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, ceist agus freagra
rules.text: A question is made with An and eclipsis (An ndúnfaidh tú? An gcuirfidh sé?). The answer repeats the verb alone, with the pronoun: Dúnfaidh mé, or in the negative Ní with lenition: Ní dhúnfaidh mé, Ní chuirfidh sé.

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, an chéad phearsa iolra
rules.text: A question put to sibh is answered in the first person plural. In Ulster the answer is analytic, verb plus muid: Dúnfaidh muid / Ní dhúnfaidh muid, Cuirfidh muid / Ní chuirfidh muid.

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, an saorbhriathar
rules.text: The autonomous form of the future is root plus -far (broad) or -fear (slender): Dúnfar an doras, Cuirfear an pláta ar an bhord. Question An ndúnfar? An gcuirfear? Negative Ní dhúnfar, Ní chuirfear.

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, briathra a thosaíonn ar ghuta
rules.text: A verb beginning with a vowel takes no prefix in the future, in the question or in the negative: Ólfaidh sé an deoch, An ólfaidh tú? Ólfaidh mé / Ní ólfaidh mé, An ólfar? Ólfar / Ní ólfar. The same holds for Úsáid, Éist, Íoc and Amharc (the usual Ulster verb for look at).

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, briathra a thosaíonn ar f
rules.text: A verb beginning with f is eclipsed after An in the question (An bhfágfaidh tú? An bhfágfar?) and lenited after Ní in the negative (Ní fhágfaidh mé, Ní fhágfar). The positive answer has no prefix: Fágfaidh mé.

rules.point: an aimsir láithreach, an chéad réimniú (achoimre)
rules.text: Verbs in a vowel or f take no prefix in the positive; f is lenited after Ní and eclipsed after An (Ní fhágaim, An bhfágann tú?). The first person singular stays synthetic in Ulster: Dúnaim, Cuirim.

rules.point: an aimsir chaite, an chéad réimniú (achoimre)
rules.text: The first person plural in Ulster is Dhún muid, Chuir muid, D'ól muid, D'úsáid muid, D'fhág muid. Autonomous Dúnadh, Cuireadh, Óladh, Úsáideadh, Fágadh. Negative Níor dhún mé, question Ar dhún tú?, both with lenition.

rules.point: an t-ainm briathartha agus an aidiacht bhriathartha, briathra leathana
rules.text: The usual pattern is verbal noun in -adh (glanadh, dúnadh) with many exceptions (fágáil, fanacht, féachaint, tógáil, ól, amharc). The verbal adjective ends in -tha after b, c, g, m, p, r (scuabtha, pioctha, leagtha, cumtha, ceaptha, gearrtha) and in -ta after d, l, n, s and ch (stadta, díolta, glanta, lasta, múchta); bh and mh become -fa (scríofa, lofa, snáfa), and a root ending in t or th simply adds -a (ata, cleachta, nochta, leata, meata). Ulster does not differ enough here to matter for a school app.

rules.point: an t-ainm briathartha agus an aidiacht bhriathartha, briathra caola
rules.text: For slender first conjugation verbs the verbal noun is usually in -eadh (briseadh, filleadh) with many exceptions (baint, bualadh, cur, rith, éisteacht, tuiscint). The verbal adjective ends in -the after b, c, g, m, p, r (béicthe, ligthe, scaipthe, tairgthe, tréigthe, rincthe) and in -te after d, l, n, s (druidte, buailte, sínte, briste); a root ending in t simply adds -e (baiste, loite, tite, scoilte), th drops before -te (caite, braite, maite, rite), and a few are irregular: cuir gives curtha, blais gives blasta, goin gives gonta, mair gives martha. Ulster does not differ enough here to matter for a school app.

lessons.title: Briathra leathana: -faidh
lessons.rule: If the last vowel of the root is broad (a, o or u), add -faidh to the root to make the future: glan becomes glanfaidh.
steps: Find the root of the verb: glan.
Look at the last vowel: a is broad, so the ending is -faidh.
Add the ending to the root: glanfaidh.
Put the verb first, then the pronoun: Glanfaidh sé an seomra ranga.

example.prompt: (Glan: sé) an seomra ranga.
example.answer: Glanfaidh sé an seomra ranga.

more.answer: Gearrfaidh sé an píotsa.
Scuabfaidh sé urlár na cistine.

lessons.hint: Broad root: root + -faidh.

lessons.title: Ceist agus freagra: An + urú, Ní + séimhiú
lessons.en: Answering a question in the future: yes and no
lessons.rule: Answer a question by repeating the verb with the right pronoun (Glanfaidh mé), and for no put Ní in front and add h (Ní ghlanfaidh mé). The question itself has An and eclipsis (An nglanfaidh tú?); l, n, r and s show no eclipsis.
steps: Take the verb from the question and remove the eclipsis: nglanfaidh becomes glanfaidh.
The question asks tú, so answer with mé: Glanfaidh mé.
For no, put Ní in front and add h: Ní ghlanfaidh mé.
Write both answers after the question: Glanfaidh mé / Ní ghlanfaidh mé.

lessons.hint: Repeat the verb for yes; Ní + h for no.

lessons.title: Briathra a thosaíonn ar ghuta nó ar f
lessons.en: Verbs beginning with a vowel or f
lessons.rule: A verb that begins with a vowel never changes after An or Ní: An ólfaidh tú? Ní ólfaidh mé. A verb that begins with f takes bhf after An and fh after Ní: An bhfágfaidh tú? Ní fhágfaidh mé.
steps: Take the verb from the question: íocfaidh.
It begins with a vowel, so nothing is added: Íocfaidh mé.
For no, put Ní in front and leave the verb as it is: Ní íocfaidh mé.
Write both answers after the question: Íocfaidh mé / Ní íocfaidh mé.

r2-chaite.title: An dara réimniú: an aimsir chaite

rules.point: an aimsir chaite, an dara réimniú, briathra leathana (-aigh)
rules.text: To put a broad second-conjugation verb (ending in -aigh) into the past tense, lenite the first consonant of the root and leave the ending as it is: brostaigh becomes bhrostaigh sé, ceannaigh becomes cheannaigh sé. The third person singular form is the lenited root with no ending added.

rules.point: an aimsir chaite, an dara réimniú, briathra caola (-igh)
rules.text: Slender second-conjugation verbs (ending in -igh) work the same way: lenite the first consonant and keep the root, so bailigh becomes bhailigh sé, mínigh becomes mhínigh sé, dúisigh becomes dhúisigh sé.

rules.point: an aimsir chaite, ceist agus diúltach: Ar, Níor
rules.text: The question is formed with Ar and the negative with Níor, both followed by lenition: Ar cheannaigh tú? Níor cheannaigh mé. The answer to a question is the verb itself, with or without Níor. For sibh the answer in Ulster usage is the analytic form with muid: Cheannaigh muid / Níor cheannaigh muid.

rules.point: an saorbhriathar, an aimsir chaite, an dara réimniú
rules.text: The free form (saorbhriathar) of the past tense is made by dropping -aigh or -igh and adding -aíodh (broad) or -íodh (slender): ceannaíodh, bailíodh. The free form is not lenited after Ar or Níor: Ar ceannaíodh? Níor ceannaíodh; Ar bailíodh? Níor bailíodh.

rules.point: an aimsir chaite, briathra a thosaíonn ar ghuta
rules.text: A second-conjugation verb beginning with a vowel takes d' in front of it in the positive past tense: d'ullmhaigh sé, d'éirigh sé, d'imigh sé. After Ar and Níor the d' is dropped: Ar ullmhaigh tú? Níor ullmhaigh mé. The free form has no d' either: Ullmhaíodh / Níor ullmhaíodh.

rules.point: an aimsir chaite, briathra a thosaíonn ar 'f'
rules.text: A second-conjugation verb beginning with f is both lenited and given d' in the positive past: d'fhiosraigh sé, d'fholmhaigh sé. After Ar and Níor the f is lenited but there is no d': Ar fhiosraigh tú? Níor fhiosraigh mé.

rules.point: an saorbhriathar, briathra a thosaíonn ar 'f'
rules.text: The free form of an f-verb keeps the plain f with no lenition and no d': Fiosraíodh an scéal; Níor fiosraíodh.

lessons.title: Séimhiú: -aigh agus -igh
lessons.rule: In the past tense, add h after the first letter and keep the whole root, ending and all: ceannaigh becomes cheannaigh, bailigh becomes bhailigh. A verb beginning with l, n, r, sc, sm, sp or st does not change: réitigh sí.
steps: Find the root of the verb in brackets: ceannaigh.
Add h after the first letter: cheannaigh.
Keep the -aigh ending as it is and put the verb first: Cheannaigh sé bainne sa siopa.

example.prompt: (Ceannaigh) sé bainne sa siopa.
example.answer: Cheannaigh sé bainne sa siopa.

more.answer: Bhailigh sé na cóipleabhair.
Chríochnaigh sé an obair.

lessons.hint: Add h after the first letter, keep the ending.

lessons.title: An diúltach le Níor
lessons.rule: To make a past-tense verb negative, put Níor in front of it and keep the h: Cheannaigh sí becomes Níor cheannaigh sí. A verb beginning with r stays as it is: Níor roghnaigh sí.
steps: Start from the positive verb: Chorraigh sé.
Keep the h that is already there: chorraigh.
Put Níor in front: Níor chorraigh sé.

example.prompt: Chorraigh sé
example.answer: Níor chorraigh sé.

more.answer: Níor dheisigh siad.
Níor shínigh sí.

lessons.hint: Níor in front, keep the h.

lessons.en: d' before a vowel and before f

r2-laithreach.title: An dara réimniú: an aimsir láithreach

rules.point: an dara réimniú, an aimsir láithreach: briathra leathana (-aigh)
rules.text: A second conjugation verb whose root ends in broad -aigh drops the -aigh and adds -aíonn for sé, sí, siad and muid: ceannaigh becomes ceannaíonn sé, críochnaigh becomes críochnaíonn sé. The first person singular ends in -aím (ceannaím). The first person plural is the analytic form with muid: ceannaíonn muid, críochnaíonn muid.

rules.point: an dara réimniú, an aimsir láithreach: briathra caola (-igh)
rules.text: A second conjugation verb whose root ends in slender -igh drops the -igh and adds -íonn: bailigh becomes bailíonn sé, mínigh becomes míníonn sé. The first person singular ends in -ím (bailím). The first person plural is bailíonn muid, míníonn muid.

rules.point: an cheist agus an diúltach san aimsir láithreach
rules.text: A question is formed with An, which eclipses the verb (An gceannaíonn tú? An mbailíonn sí?), and the negative with Ní, which lenites it (Ní cheannaíonn sé, Ní bhailíonn siad). There is no separate word for yes or no; the answer repeats the verb in the right person: Ceannaím / Ní cheannaím.

rules.point: an freagra: athrú pearsan
rules.text: When a question is answered the person changes: a question with tú is answered with the -ím form (An mbailíonn tú? Bailím) and a question with sibh with the muid form (An mbailíonn sibh? Bailíonn muid). Questions with sé, sí and siad keep the same pronoun in the answer.

rules.point: briathra sa dara réimniú a thosaíonn ar ghuta
rules.text: A verb beginning with a vowel is written unchanged after both An and Ní in the present tense: An ullmhaíonn tú? Ullmhaím / Ní ullmhaím; An aimsíonn sé? Ní aimsíonn sé. No h or n is prefixed.

rules.point: briathra sa dara réimniú a thosaíonn ar f
rules.text: A verb beginning with f takes bhf after An (An bhfiosraíonn tú?) and fh after Ní (Ní fhiosraíonn sé), so the f is silent in both the question and the negative.

rules.point: an saorbhriathar, an aimsir láithreach
rules.text: The free (autonomous) form ends in -aítear for broad verbs and -ítear for slender verbs: ceannaítear, ullmhaítear, bailítear, deisítear na gluaisteáin. It is questioned and negated like the other forms: An gceannaítear? Ceannaítear / Ní cheannaítear; An bhfiosraítear? Ní fhiosraítear.

rules.point: forainm réamhfhoclach sa fhreagra
rules.text: When an order containing a prepositional pronoun is reported, that pronoun agrees with the new subject: the order Imigh leat becomes Imíonn sé leis (and Imíonn sí léi, Imíonn muid linn).

rules.point: nóta Ultach: an chéad phearsa iolra agus Céard
rules.text: The column heading Céard a dhéanann sé? is given as Cad é a dhéanann sé?

lessons.title: -aíonn agus -íonn
lessons.rule: Drop -aigh and add -aíonn, or drop -igh and add -íonn, then put the subject: ceannaigh becomes ceannaíonn sé, bailigh becomes bailíonn sé. To answer a question about someone else, drop An and the eclipsis and keep the same subject: An gceannaíonn sé? Ceannaíonn sé. / Ní cheannaíonn sé.
steps: Find the verb in the question: gceannaíonn, from ceannaigh.
Take off An and the eclipsis: ceannaíonn.
Keep sé and the rest of the sentence: Ceannaíonn sé ticéad ar an bhus. For no, put Ní in front and add h: Ní cheannaíonn sé ticéad ar an bhus.

lessons.title: -aím agus -ím: ceist a fhreagairt
lessons.rule: To answer a question with tú, use the mé ending, -aím for a broad verb and -ím for a slender one, with no pronoun after it: An gceannaíonn tú? Ceannaím. / Ní cheannaím. Change do to mo and ort to orm.
steps: Take An and the eclipsis off the verb: gcríochnaíonn becomes críochnaíonn.
Swap -aíonn for -aím and drop tú: críochnaím.
Change d' to m' and write the answer: Críochnaím m'obair bhaile roimh an dinnéar. For no, put Ní in front and add h: Ní chríochnaím m'obair bhaile roimh an dinnéar.

lessons.title: Ceist le An, diúltach le Ní
lessons.en: Questions with An, negatives with Ní
lessons.rule: For a question put An before the verb and eclipse it (An gceannaíonn, An bhfiosraíonn); for a negative put Ní and lenite it (Ní cheannaíonn, Ní fhiosraíonn). m and s do not change after An: An míníonn sí?
steps: Start from the answer: Tosaím.
Change the mé ending back to -aíonn: tosaíonn.
Put An in front and eclipse the t: An dtosaíonn.
The answer used mé, so ask with tú: An dtosaíonn tú ar an obair bhaile go luath?

r2-fhaistineach.title: An dara réimniú: an aimsir fháistineach

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, an dara réimniú, briathra leathana (-aigh)
rules.text: For a broad second-conjugation verb, drop the -aigh of the root and add -óidh: brostaigh gives brostóidh sé, ceannaigh gives ceannóidh mé.

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, an dara réimniú, briathra caola (-igh)
rules.text: For a slender second-conjugation verb, drop the -igh and add -eoidh: bailigh gives baileoidh sé, mínigh gives míneoidh sé, dúisigh gives dúiseoidh sé.

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, ceist agus diúltach
rules.text: The question is formed with An and eclipsis (An gceannóidh tú? An mbaileoidh sé?) and the negative with Ní and lenition (Ní cheannóidh mé, Ní bhaileoidh mé). The answer repeats the verb: Ceannóidh mé / Ní cheannóidh mé.

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, an chéad phearsa iolra
rules.text: In Ulster usage the first person plural is analytic, verb plus muid: ceannóidh muid, baileoidh muid, ní cheannóidh muid, ní bhaileoidh muid. The question with sibh is answered Ceannóidh muid / Ní cheannóidh muid.

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, an saorbhriathar
rules.text: The autonomous form ends in -ófar for broad verbs and -eofar for slender verbs: ceannófar, baileofar. It takes eclipsis after An (An gceannófar?) and lenition after Ní (Ní cheannófar).

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, briathra a thosaíonn ar ghuta
rules.text: A second-conjugation verb beginning with a vowel behaves the same in the future (aeraigh gives aeróidh, éirigh gives éireoidh) but takes no d' and shows no change after An or Ní: An ullmhóidh tú? Ní ullmhóidh mé, An aimseoidh sé? Ní aimseoidh sé, An ullmhófar? Ní ullmhófar.

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, briathra a thosaíonn ar f
rules.text: A second-conjugation verb beginning with f takes the eclipsis bhf after An (An bhfiosróidh tú? An bhfiosrófar?) and the lenition fh after Ní (Ní fhiosróidh mé, Ní fhiosrófar).

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, clásal le má agus nuair a
rules.text: Where the má clause has a synthetic first person plural (má chuirimid, má dhéanaimid, má théimid) Ulster usage is analytic: má chuireann muid, má dhéanann muid, má théann muid. The pupil changes only the bracketed verb.

rules.point: an dara réimniú, achoimre ar na haimsirí (láithreach, caite, fháistineach)
rules.text: Present: -aím / -ím with the -aíonn / -íonn endings and the autonomous -aítear / -ítear, the first person plural in Ulster being ceannaíonn muid rather than ceannaímid; past: the root lenited, d' before a vowel or f (D'ullmhaigh, D'fhiosraigh), the autonomous -aíodh / -íodh, Níor / Ar, and in Ulster cheannaigh muid rather than cheannaíomar; future: -óidh / -eoidh, the autonomous -ófar / -eofar, Ní / An, and in Ulster ceannóidh muid rather than ceannóimid. The first person singular stays synthetic in every tense: ceannaím, cheannaigh mé, ceannóidh mé.

rules.point: an dara réimniú, an chéad phearsa iolra san aimsir chaite
rules.text: The table gives the past first person plural synthetically: Cheannaíomar, Bhailíomar, D'ullmhaíomar, D'aimsíomar, D'fhiosraíomar. In Ulster usage these are analytic: cheannaigh muid, bhailigh muid, d'ullmhaigh muid, d'aimsigh muid, d'fhiosraigh muid; negative níor cheannaigh muid, question ar cheannaigh sibh?

rules.point: an t-ainm briathartha, briathra leathana an dara réimniú
rules.text: The verbal noun of a broad -aigh verb is usually formed by replacing -aigh with -ú (aeraigh: aerú, ceartaigh: ceartú, socraigh: socrú). The list marks the exceptions ending in -ach (ceannach, clúdach, cnuasach, cuardach, cumhdach, fuadach), in -aí (corraí, fiafraí, ionsaí) and admháil.

rules.point: an aidiacht bhriathartha, briathra leathana an dara réimniú
rules.text: The verbal adjective of a broad -aigh verb replaces -aigh with -aithe (ceannaithe, críochnaithe, socraithe). The one exception in the list is dathaigh: daite.

rules.point: an t-ainm briathartha agus an aidiacht bhriathartha, briathra caola an dara réimniú
rules.text: The verbal noun of a slender -igh verb is usually -iú (aimsiú, ceistiú, deisiú, míniú) and the verbal adjective -ithe (aimsithe, deisithe, mínithe). The list marks the exceptions: biseach, coinneáil, cuimhneamh, dúiseacht, éirí, glinniúint, imeacht, impí, réiteach, taifeach.

lessons.title: Briathra a thosaíonn ar ghuta nó ar f
lessons.en: Verbs beginning with a vowel or f: nothing in front
lessons.rule: A verb that begins with a vowel or f takes the same ending as any other, and nothing goes in front of it: there is no d' in the future (D'ullmhaigh sí in the past, but Ullmhóidh sí).
steps: Find the root of the verb: aeraigh.
Take away -aigh and add -óidh: aeróidh.
Put nothing in front of it, not even d': Aeróidh sé an seomra ranga ag am lóin.

lessons.title: An fhoirm dhiúltach: Ní + séimhiú
lessons.en: Saying what will not happen: Ní + lenition
lessons.rule: To make the future negative, put Ní in front of the verb and add h after the first letter: ceannóidh becomes Ní cheannóidh. Verbs that begin with l, n or r show no change (Ní laghdóidh).

Put Ní in front of it.
Add h after the first letter: Ní cheannóidh mé aip nua don fhón.

lessons.title: An fhoirm cheisteach: An + urú
lessons.rule: To write the question for an answer, put An in front of the verb and eclipse it (ceannóidh becomes An gceannóidh), and swap mé for tú or muid for sibh. Verbs that begin with l, n, r or s show no eclipsis (An socróidh sí?).
steps: Find the verb in the answer: Baileoidh.
Put An in front and eclipse it: b takes m, so An mbaileoidh.
The answer says mé, so the question asks tú: An mbaileoidh tú na fóin ag tús an ranga?

steps: Find the verb: Aimseoidh.
Put Ní in front of it.
It begins with a vowel, so leave it as it is: Ní aimseoidh sé a fhón sa mhála.

lessons.title: An saorbhriathar: -ófar
lessons.rule: When you do not say who does the action, take away -aigh and add -ófar, with no pronoun after it: ceannaigh becomes ceannófar.
steps: Find the root: ceannaigh.
Take away -aigh and add -ófar: ceannófar.
Put it first, with no pronoun after it: Ceannófar fón nua roimh dheireadh na míosa.

nr-chaite.title: Na briathra neamhrialta: an aimsir chaite

rules.point: na briathra neamhrialta, an aimsir chaite: an fhoirm dhiúltach agus an fhoirm cheisteach
rules.text: The other six take ní and an with a separate dependent form: ní dhearna, an ndearna; ní fhaca, an bhfaca; ní dúirt, an ndúirt; ní dheachaigh, an ndeachaigh; ní bhfuair, an bhfuair; ní raibh, an raibh. With muid the same pattern holds: níor rug muid, ar rug muid; ní dhearna muid, an ndearna muid.

rules.point: na briathra neamhrialta, an aimsir chaite: freagra ar cheist
rules.text: A yes or no question in the past tense is answered by repeating the verb in the positive or negative form, without a word for yes or no: Ar tháinig tú ar scoil ar do rothar? Tháinig mé. Níor tháinig mé. An bhfaca tú an scannán sin? Chonaic mé. Ní fhaca mé.

rules.point: na briathra neamhrialta, an aimsir chaite: an saorbhriathar
rules.text: Each irregular verb has a past-tense autonomous form: rugadh, chualathas, thángthas, itheadh, tugadh, rinneadh, chonacthas, dúradh, chuathas, fuarthas, bhíothas. The negative and question forms use the same particle as the verb itself takes: níor rugadh, ar rugadh; ní dhearnadh, an ndearnadh; ní fhacthas, an bhfacthas; ní dúradh, an ndúradh; ní dheachthas, an ndeachthas; ní bhfuarthas, an bhfuarthas; ní rabhthas, an rabhthas.

rules.point: na briathra neamhrialta, an aimsir chaite: an chéad phearsa iolra (nóta Uladh, ní ón leabhar)
rules.text: Vocabulary changed: ag féachaint ar becomes ag amharc ar, le déanaí becomes ar na mallaibh, fós becomes go fóill.

lessons.en: The negative with Níor: five irregular verbs
lessons.rule: Five irregular verbs, beir, cluin, tar, ith and tabhair, make the negative like regular verbs: put Níor in front of the past form (rug, chuala, tháinig, thug), and D'ith loses its d': Níor ith.
steps: Find the past verb: Thug.
It is one of the five Níor verbs, so put Níor in front: Níor thug.
Keep the rest of the sentence: Níor thug Mamaí an t-airgead dom.

lessons.title: Ní: déan, feic, abair, téigh, faigh, bí
lessons.en: The negative with Ní: six irregular verbs
lessons.rule: Six irregular verbs use Ní and a special negative form that you learn by heart: rinne becomes ní dhearna, chonaic ní fhaca, dúirt ní dúirt, chuaigh ní dheachaigh, fuair ní bhfuair, bhí ní raibh. In Ulster you will also hear níor dhúirt.

lessons.rule: When nobody is named as doing the action, use the verb's own autonomous form, learnt by heart: rugadh, chualathas, thángthas, itheadh, tugadh, rinneadh, chonacthas, dúradh, chuathas, fuarthas, bhíothas. For a question use the particle the verb always takes: Ar tugadh? An ndearnadh?

nr-laithreach.title: Na briathra neamhrialta: an aimsir láithreach

rules.point: na briathra neamhrialta, an aimsir láithreach: na haon bhriathar déag
rules.text: The first person singular keeps the synthetic ending -im (beirim, cloisim, tagaim), the other persons take -eann/-ann with a pronoun, and the first person plural is analytic: beireann muid, cloiseann muid, tagann muid, tá muid, not beirimid, cloisimid, tagaimid, táimid.

rules.point: an aimsir láithreach, an fhoirm cheisteach: An + urú
rules.text: A present-tense question is formed with An followed by eclipsis of the verb: An mbeireann, An gcloiseann, An dtagann, An dtugann, An ndéanann, An bhfeiceann, An ndeir, An dtéann, An bhfaigheann. A verb beginning with a vowel takes no change (An itheann), and bí has its own dependent form (An bhfuil). Note that feic uses the dependent form after An even in Ulster: the answer is Tchím or Tchí sé, but the question is An bhfeiceann tú? and An bhfeiceann sé?

rules.point: an aimsir láithreach, an fhoirm dhiúltach: Ní + séimhiú
rules.text: The negative is formed with Ní followed by lenition of the verb: Ní bheireann, Ní chloiseann, Ní thagann, Ní thugann, Ní dhéanann, Ní fheiceann, Ní théann, Ní fhaigheann. Deir is not lenited (Ní deir), a vowel takes no change (Ní itheann), and bí has the separate negative form Níl. Feic again uses the dependent form after Ní: Tchí sé but Ní fheiceann sé.

rules.point: an aimsir láithreach, freagra gairid
rules.text: A yes/no question is answered by repeating the verb with the pronoun, without any word for yes or no: An gcloiseann sé? gives Cloiseann sé or Ní chloiseann sé; An bhfuil sé go maith? gives Tá sé or Níl sé. With feic the positive answer is the independent Ulster form and the negative the dependent one: An bhfeiceann tú? gives Tchím or Ní fheicim; An bhfeiceann sé? gives Tchí sé or Ní fheiceann sé. In the first person plural the answer is Cloiseann muid, Tá muid, Níl muid.

rules.point: an aimsir láithreach, an saorbhriathar
rules.text: Its negative and question forms follow the same rules as the rest of the verb: Ní bheirtear, An mbeirtear? and, for bí, Níltear. Feictear is the form to teach; the Ulster tchítear is also heard.

rules.point: an aimsir láithreach, bí: tá, níl, an bhfuil
rules.text: Bí is the only verb with three distinct present forms: tá in the positive, níl in the negative and bhfuil after the question particle An.

lessons.title: An fhoirm dhiúltach: Ní + séimhiú
lessons.en: Saying what does not happen: Ní + lenition
lessons.rule: To make a present-tense verb negative, put Ní in front of it and add h after the first letter: tagann becomes Ní thagann. Deir and verbs that begin with a vowel do not change (Ní deir, Ní itheann), and tá becomes Níl.
steps: Find the verb at the start of the sentence: Déanann.
Put Ní in front of it.
Add h after the first letter: Ní dhéanann.
Keep the rest of the sentence as it was: Ní dhéanann sí a dícheall sa rang Gaeilge.

lessons.title: An fhoirm cheisteach: An + urú
lessons.rule: To turn a sentence into a question, put An in front of the verb and eclipse it: tagann becomes An dtagann, beireann becomes An mbeireann. If the sentence has Ní, take away Ní and its h first; a vowel does not change (An itheann), and deir becomes An ndeir.
steps: Find the verb: Tagann.
Put An in front of it.
Eclipse the verb: t takes d, so An dtagann.
Keep the rest and add a question mark: An dtagann sé ar scoil ar an bhus?

lessons.hint: An + eclipsis: b to mb, c to gc, d to nd, f to bhf, g to ng, p to bp, t to dt.

lessons.title: Ceist le tú agus sibh
lessons.en: Asking you: swap mé for tú and muid for sibh
lessons.rule: When the sentence is about me or us, the question is put to you: change the -im form to the verb with tú (Déanaim becomes An ndéanann tú?) and muid to sibh (Téann muid becomes An dtéann sibh?). Tá mé becomes An bhfuil tú?
steps: Find the verb and who does it: Itheann muid.
The question is put to the group, so change muid to sibh: Itheann sibh.
Put An in front; a vowel takes no eclipsis: An itheann sibh.
Keep the rest and add a question mark: An itheann sibh lón sa cheaintín?

lessons.title: Freagra gairid: dearfach agus diúltach
lessons.rule: Irish has no word for yes or no: for yes, repeat the verb with its subject (Cluinim), and for no, put Ní in front and add h (Ní chluinim). A question to tú is answered with the -im form, and the question An bhfeiceann tú? is answered Tchím or Ní fheicim.
steps: Take the verb from the question and remove the eclipsis: gcluineann becomes cluineann.
For yes, repeat it with the pronoun: Cluineann sé.
For no, put Ní in front and add h: Ní chluineann sé.
Write both answers after the question: Cluineann sé. / Ní chluineann sé.

lessons.title: An saorbhriathar
lessons.en: The autonomous form: when nobody is named
lessons.rule: When you do not say who does the action, use the autonomous form, which ends in -tar, -tear or -ear and has no pronoun after it: tugann becomes Tugtar, cluineann becomes Cluintear. Learn the forms from the tables: beirtear, cluintear, tagtar, itear, tugtar, déantar, feictear, deirtear, téitear, faightear.
steps: Find the verb in brackets: téigh.
Take its autonomous present form: téitear.
Put it first, with no pronoun after it: Téitear chuig an Ghaeltacht achan samhradh.

nr-fhaistineach.title: Na briathra neamhrialta: an aimsir fháistineach

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, an fhoirm dhiúltach
rules.text: The negative is formed with ní, which lenites the verb (ní chloisfidh, ní thiocfaidh, ní thabharfaidh, ní dhéanfaidh, ní fheicfidh, ní bhéarfaidh, ní bheidh). Ní does not change déarfaidh or rachaidh, and it cannot lenite a vowel (ní íosfaidh); faigh alone uses its dependent form with eclipsis after ní: ní bhfaighidh.

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, an fhoirm cheisteach
rules.text: The question is formed with an, which eclipses the verb (an gcloisfidh, an dtiocfaidh, an mbéarfaidh, an ndéanfaidh, an dtabharfaidh, an bhfeicfidh, an ndéarfaidh, an mbeidh). Rachaidh and íosfaidh are unchanged after an, and faigh again takes its dependent form: an bhfaighidh.

rules.point: an aimsir fháistineach, an saorbhriathar
rules.text: Faigh has gheofar in the positive but ní bhfaighfear and an bhfaighfear in the negative and question. Negative and question forms follow the same lenition and eclipsis pattern as the personal forms.

rules.point: freagra ar cheist san aimsir fháistineach
rules.text: A yes or no question is answered by repeating the verb in its positive or negative form with the right pronoun (An dtiocfaidh tú liom? Tiocfaidh mé. Ní thiocfaidh mé.); there is no separate word for yes or no. A question to sibh is answered with muid: An rachaidh sibh? Rachaidh muid. Ní rachaidh muid.

rules.point: an chéad phearsa iolra: foirmeacha Uladh
rules.text: In Ulster the analytic form is used: béarfaidh muid, cloisfidh muid, tiocfaidh muid, íosfaidh muid, tabharfaidh muid, déanfaidh muid, feicfidh muid, déarfaidh muid, rachaidh muid, gheobhaidh muid, beidh muid; negative ní bhéarfaidh muid, ní bhfaighidh muid, ní bheidh muid; question an mbéarfaidh muid?, an mbeidh muid?

rules.point: botúin chló sa tábla ar leathanach 58 (le seiceáil)
rules.text: Under Tar the question column reads An gcloisfear? where An dtiocfaidh mé? is meant; under Feic the first form is printed Feicidh mé for Feicfidh mé and the question column reads An bhfeicfear? where An bhfeicfidh mé? is meant; under Téigh the question column reads An rachfar? where An rachaidh mé? is meant; under Faigh the tú and sibh forms are printed Geobhaidh without lenition; the question An íosfar lacks its question mark. Also on page 55 question 6 is printed in the conditional (An íosfadh tú ... Ní íosfadh mé) where the future íosfaidh is meant.

rules.point: urú i ndiaidh réamhfhocail agus an ailt sna ceachtanna (le seiceáil)
rules.text: In the Ulster versions these become ar an bhata and ag an chruinniú, following the school rule that a simple preposition and the singular article lenite (ar an bhord, ag an doras, sa charr, leis an mhúinteoir). The fresh sentences use the Ulster pattern throughout (ag an chluiche, ar an bhus, ar an ghadaí).

lessons.title: Foirmeacha an bhriathair
lessons.en: The future forms of the irregular verbs
lessons.rule: Each irregular verb has its own future form, which you learn from the table (beir: béarfaidh, ith: íosfaidh, tar: tiocfaidh, téigh: rachaidh, faigh: gheobhaidh, bí: beidh). Put that form first, then the subject.
steps: Find the verb in brackets: tabhair.
Look up its future form: tabharfaidh.
Put it first, then the pronoun sé: Tabharfaidh sé an ticéad dom.

example.answer: Tabharfaidh sé an ticéad dom.

lessons.title: Freagra gairid: dearfach agus diúltach
lessons.rule: Irish has no word for yes or no: repeat the verb with the pronoun for yes (Tiocfaidh mé) and put Ní in front for no (Ní thiocfaidh mé). For faigh the answers are Gheobhaidh mé and Ní bhfaighidh mé.
steps: Take the verb from the question and remove the eclipsis: gcluinfidh becomes cluinfidh.
For yes, repeat it with the pronoun: Cluinfidh sí.
For no, put Ní in front and add h: Ní chluinfidh sí.
Write both answers after the question: (a) Cluinfidh sí. (b) Ní chluinfidh sí.

lessons.title: Ceist a scríobh: An + urú
lessons.rule: To write the question, take away Ní and its h, put An in front and eclipse the verb (An dtiocfaidh?); gheobhaidh becomes An bhfaighidh, and rachaidh and vowels do not change. If the answer says mé, the question asks tú.

Put An in front and eclipse it: d takes n, so An ndéarfaidh.
Keep the rest and add a question mark: An ndéarfaidh sí leis an mhúinteoir é?

lessons.en: The autonomous form: when nobody is named
lessons.rule: When you do not say who does the action, use the autonomous form with no pronoun after it: cluin becomes cluinfear, faigh becomes gheofar, bí becomes beifear.

rules.point: an aidiacht shealbhach, mo, do, a (sé): séimhiú
rules.text: The possessive adjectives mo (my), do (your, singular) and a (his) lenite the first consonant of the following noun: mo theach, do chóta, a bhróga.

rules.point: an aidiacht shealbhach, mo agus do roimh ghuta
rules.text: Before a vowel or fh, mo and do drop their vowel and become m' and d': m'fhiacail, m'uncail, m'aintín, d'athair.

rules.point: an aidiacht shealbhach, a (sí): h roimh ghuta
rules.text: The possessive a meaning her causes no change to a consonant (a cara, a bronntanas) but puts h before a vowel: a hordóg.

rules.point: an aidiacht shealbhach, a (sé) roimh ghuta
rules.text: The possessive a meaning his causes no change before a vowel: a ordóg.

rules.point: an aidiacht shealbhach, ár, bhur, a (siad): urú
rules.text: The plural possessives ár (our), bhur (your, plural) and a (their) eclipse the following consonant: ár gcóipleabhair, bhur dtuismitheoirí, a gcótaí. Before a vowel they add n- (written nA without a hyphen before a capital): ár nAthair, bhur n-aintín, a n-uncail.

rules.point: an aidiacht shealbhach le hainmneacha briathartha staide: i mo chónaí, ina suí
rules.text: The states cónaí, dúiseacht, suí, seasamh, tost, luí and codladh are expressed with the preposition i plus the possessive adjective: i mo, i do, ina (his and her), inár, in bhur (also written i bhur), ina (their). The usual lenition, h and eclipsis rules of the possessives apply: i mo chónaí, ina chónaí, ina cónaí, inár gcónaí, ina gcodladh. In Ulster the first person plural verb is analytic: tá muid inár gcónaí, not táimid inár gcónaí.

lessons.title: M' agus d' roimh ghuta
lessons.en: My and your before a vowel
lessons.rule: Before a vowel, mo becomes m' and do becomes d', joined to the noun: m'uncail, d'athair. A noun beginning with f first takes h, then counts as a vowel: m'fhón, d'fhoirm.
steps: Add h after the f, as after any mo: fón becomes fhón.
fh makes no sound, so the word now begins with a vowel sound: mo becomes m'.
Join them and write the sentence: Seo é m'fhón póca.

lessons.rule: After a meaning her, a consonant does not change (a cara), but a vowel takes h in front (a haintín). The same goes for lena (with her): lena haintín.

lessons.title: Ár, bhur, a (siad): urú
lessons.rule: After ár (our), bhur (your, plural) and a (their), eclipse the noun: mb, gc, nd, bhf, ng, bp, dt, and n- before a vowel. Nouns beginning with l, m, n, r or s do not change.
steps: Find the word before the brackets: bhur (your, plural).
Eclipse the first letter: t takes d in front, so ticéid becomes dticéid.
Write the sentence: Cá bhfuil bhur dticéid, a pháistí?

lessons.title: I mo chónaí, ina shuí
lessons.en: Saying where or how someone is: i mo chónaí
lessons.rule: To say someone lives somewhere or is sitting, standing, lying, asleep, awake or silent, use tá + i mo, i do, ina, inár or in bhur + the state word (cónaí, suí, seasamh, luí, codladh, dúiseacht, tost). Then change the state word as after the possessive: ina shuí (his), ina suí (her), ina gcodladh (their).
steps: Find the person: sé (he), so ina means his.
After his, add h after the first letter: suí becomes shuí.
Write the sentence: Tá sé ina shuí ar an bhus.

rules.point: na maoluimhreacha: cruth agus úsáid
rules.text: Counting numbers used on their own take the particle a before them (a haon, a dó) and a vowel-initial number takes h (a haon, a hocht); 11 to 19 add déag (a dó dhéag is lenited), 20 is fiche and 21 is fiche a haon. These forms are used for labels such as rang a trí, seomra a hocht, bus a hocht and, in a Northern Ireland school, Bliain a hocht for Year 8. Ulster usage is the same as the standard.

rules.point: na deicheanna agus an céad
rules.text: The tens are deich, fiche, tríocha, daichead, caoga, seasca, seachtó, ochtó, nócha and céad, and a noun following a ten is unchanged (fiche punt, seasca punt, seachtó pingin), while deich eclipses (deich bpunt, deich bpingin). Ulster usage is the same as the standard.

rules.point: an mhatamaitic: suimiú, dealú, iolrú, roinnt
rules.text: Sums are read with is for plus (a seacht is a dó), óna for minus (a trí óna hocht), faoina for times (a sé faoina trí), ar for divided by (fiche ar a dó) and sin for equals. Ulster usage is the same as the standard; roinnte ar is also heard for divided by.

rules.point: an t-am: an uair a chlog
rules.text: The hours are given as Tá sé a haon a chlog, Tá sé a dó a chlog and so on up to a dó dhéag a chlog; the counting form with a is used, with h before aon and ocht. Ulster usage is the same as the standard.

rules.point: an t-am: leathuair, ceathrú, bomaite
rules.text: Minutes past the hour use tar éis (leathuair tar éis a deich, ceathrú tar éis a naoi) and minutes to the hour use chun (fiche bomaite chun a trí, cúig bhomaite chun a cúig); the word bomaite may be left out. Ulster uses bomaite where the standard has nóiméad: it is lenited after 2 to 6 (cúig bhomaite) and eclipsed after 7 to 10 (deich mbomaite).

rules.point: na bunuimhreacha: séimhiú agus urú ar an ainmfhocal
rules.text: A noun after a cardinal number stays singular. One is aon chapall amháin or capall amháin; 2 to 6 lenite (dhá chapall, sé chapall); 7 to 9 eclipse (seacht gcapall, naoi gcapall); deich also eclipses (deich gcapall) and is listed as an exception to the 7 to 9 rule. Ulster usage is the same as the standard.

rules.point: na bunuimhreacha: 11 go 19, 20 agus os a chionn
rules.text: For 11 to 19 the noun sits between the number and déag (aon chapall déag, seacht gcapall déag); 20 is fiche capall with no mutation; above 20 the unit and noun come first and the ten follows with is (aon chapall is fiche or capall is fiche, ocht gcapall is tríocha, trí chapall is caoga). Ulster usage is the same as the standard.

rules.point: na bunuimhreacha: ainmfhocail a thosaíonn ar ghuta
rules.text: A vowel-initial noun is unchanged after 2 to 6 (dhá úll, trí iasc, sé uan) but takes n- after 7 to 9 (seacht n-úll, ocht n-iasc, naoi n-uan). Ulster usage is the same as the standard.

rules.point: na bunuimhreacha: dhá agus ceithre i gcomparáid
rules.text: The picture captions contrast dhá bhuidéal with dhá iasc and ceithre chos with ceithre úll to show that 2 to 6 lenite a consonant but leave a vowel untouched. Ulster usage is the same as the standard.

rules.point: airgead: punt agus pingin
rules.text: Prices are read with the noun singular after the number: punt (amháin), ceithre phunt, sé phunt nócha a naoi for £6.99, deich bpingin for 10p, cúig phunt déag for £15. The Ulster question is Cá mhéad atá air?.

rules.point: na horduimhreacha 1ú go 20ú
rules.text: Ordinals are an chéad chapall (chéad lenites the noun), an dara, an tríú, an ceathrú, an cúigiú, an séú, an seachtú, an t-ochtú, an naoú, an deichiú; a vowel-initial ordinal takes t- after an (an t-aonú, an t-ochtú). From 11th to 19th the ordinal comes first and déag follows the noun (an t-aonú capall déag, an dóú capall déag); 20th is an fichiú capall. Ulster usage is the same as the standard.

rules.point: na horduimhreacha os cionn 20
rules.text: Above 20 the unit ordinal comes first, then the noun, then is and the ten (an t-aonú capall is fiche, an dara capall is fiche, an tríú capall is tríocha, an t-ochtú capall is daichead). The tens are an tríochadú, an daicheadú, an caogadú, an seascadú, an seachtódú, an t-ochtódú, an nóchadú and an céadú capall. Ulster usage is the same as the standard.

rules.point: na huimhreacha pearsanta 1 go 14
rules.text: People are counted with the personal numbers duine, beirt, triúr, ceathrar, cúigear, seisear, seachtar, ochtar, naonúr, deichniúr; from 11 the ordinary numbers are used with duine and dhéag: aon duine dhéag, dáréag (12), trí dhuine dhéag, ceithre dhuine dhéag. Ulster usage is the same as the standard.

rules.point: na huimhreacha pearsanta le hainmfhocal
rules.text: A noun after a personal number is in the genitive plural: beirt lenites (beirt fhear, beirt bhan) but triúr to deichniúr do not (triúr fear, ceathrar ban, deichniúr fear). From 11 the ordinary cardinals are used with the noun singular: aon fhear déag, dáréag fear, trí fhear déag, seacht bhfear déag, fiche fear. Ulster usage is the same as the standard; gasúr and girseach may be used beside buachaill and cailín (beirt ghasúr, triúr girseach).

rules.point: na huimhreacha pearsanta os cionn 20
rules.text: Above 20 people are counted with the ordinary cardinals and duine: duine is fiche, trí dhuine is tríocha, ceithre dhuine is daichead, seacht nduine is caoga, naoi nduine is seasca, ocht nduine is ochtó, céad duine. Ulster usage is the same as the standard.

rules.point: na dátaí
rules.text: A date is the ordinal, lá, then de and the month lenited: an tríú lá de Mhárta, an cúigiú lá déag de Bhealtaine; the same pattern serves for other months (d'Eanáir, d'Fheabhra, de Nollaig). Ulster usage is the same as the standard.

rules.point: na horduimhreacha: cibé athrú is gá
rules.text: When an ordinal is written out after an, the necessary changes are: t- before a vowel-initial ordinal (an t-aonú, an t-ochtú), lenition of the noun after an chéad (an chéad duais) and h before a vowel-initial noun after other ordinals (an fichiú huair, an t-aonú himleabhar déag). Ulster usage is the same as the standard.

rules.point: an dobhriathar: treo agus suíomh
rules.text: Irish uses different adverbs for the direction of a movement and for the position where something rests afterwards. The section (subtitled Treo agus suíomh) teaches four groups of these adverbs through pairs of pictures: one showing the movement, the next showing the resting position. Ulster Irish uses exactly the same ten adverbs with the same meanings.

rules.point: suas, thuas, anuas
rules.text: Suas is used for movement upwards away from the speaker (Tá Pól ag dul suas an staighre); thuas for being at rest up above (tá sé thuas staighre); anuas for movement downwards towards the speaker from above (Tá sé ag teacht anuas).

rules.point: síos, thíos, aníos
rules.text: Síos is used for movement downwards away from the speaker (ag dul síos go bun an chnoic); thíos for being at rest down below (tá sí thíos ag bun an chnoic); aníos for movement upwards towards the speaker from below (ag teacht aníos arís).

rules.point: isteach, istigh
rules.text: Isteach is used for movement into a place (Chuaigh Aoife isteach sa teach); istigh for being at rest inside (Anois tá sí istigh).

rules.point: amach, amuigh
rules.text: Amach is used for movement out of a place (Shiúil Máirtín amach as an teach); amuigh for being at rest outside (tá sé amuigh sa ghairdín).

rules.point: nóta eagarthóireachta
rules.text: Newry is written An tIúr (go dtí an tIúr) in the fresh sentences.

r1-coinniollach.title: An chéad réimniú: an modh coinníollach

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, an chéad réimniú, briathra leathana
rules.text: To form the conditional of a broad first-conjugation verb, lenite the initial consonant and add -fadh to the root for the third person (dún becomes dhúnfadh sé). in Ulster usage.

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, foircinn na mbriathra leathana
rules.text: The broad endings are -fainn (mé), -fá (tú), -fadh sé / sí, -fadh muid, -fadh sibh, -faidís (siad) and -faí (saorbhriathar). Questions to sibh are answered with the muid form (An ndúnfadh sibh? Dhúnfadh muid). Only the first person singular keeps a synthetic ending in Ulster school usage.

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, an chéad réimniú, briathra caola
rules.text: A slender-root verb takes the same endings spelt slender: -feadh (chuirfeadh sé), -finn, -feá, -feadh muid, -fidís, -fí.

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, ceist agus diúltach
rules.text: A question is formed with An plus eclipsis (An ndúnfá? An gcuirfeá?) and the negative with Ní plus lenition (Ní dhúnfainn, Ní chuirfinn). Yes and no answers repeat the verb in the right person.

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, briathra a thosaíonn ar ghuta
rules.text: A verb beginning with a vowel takes d' in the positive (D'ólfadh sé, D'úsáidfeadh sé) but drops it after An and Ní (An ólfá? D'ólfainn / Ní ólfainn).

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, briathra a thosaíonn ar f
rules.text: A verb beginning with f takes d' plus lenition in the positive (D'fhágfadh sé), eclipsis after An (An bhfágfá?) and lenition without d' after Ní (Ní fhágfainn).

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, an saorbhriathar
rules.text: The autonomous form ends in -faí (broad) or -fí (slender), is lenited in the positive, and takes d' before a vowel or f (Dhúnfaí, Chuirfí, D'ólfaí, D'fhágfaí; Ní dhúnfaí, Ní ólfaí).

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, clásal le dá
rules.text: A condition introduced by dá takes the conditional in both halves: Dá mbeadh tart orm d'ólfainn tae; Dá mbeinn tinn d'fhanfainn sa leaba; dá mbeifeá tinn; dá mbeidís go maith. These forms of bí are the same in Ulster school usage.

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, an fhoirm dhiúltach
rules.text: To make a conditional form negative, put Ní before it, remove any d' and lenite the initial consonant: Mholfadh muid becomes Ní mholfadh muid, D'éistfidís becomes Ní éistfidís, D'fhéachfadh sé becomes Ní fhéachfadh sé (in Ulster the verb amharc is more usual than féach: D'amharcfadh sé, Ní amharcfadh sé).

rules.point: nóta Uladh: an chéad phearsa iolra
rules.text: The first person singular -fainn / -finn stays synthetic. Still for sign-off.

rules.point: nóta Uladh: urú i ndiaidh an ailt
rules.text: Applied throughout the Ulster fields: ar an bhord, ar an chlár dubh, ar an phictiúr, sa charr, leis an cheol, as an bhus; d, t and s stay unchanged (ar an doras, ar an teilifís, sa teach). Céard a dhéanfadh sé? and Cad a dhéanfá? become Cad é a dhéanfadh sé? and Cad é a dhéanfá?.

rules.point: nóta eagarthóireachta: earráidí cló sa leabhar
rules.text: The data reads na soilse, na seomraí, ar an teilifís, an císte and Dá mbeadh. Confirm at sign-off.

lessons.title: Séimhiú agus -fadh / -feadh
lessons.rule: To say what someone would do, put séimhiú on the verb and add -fadh to a broad root or -feadh to a slender root: glan becomes ghlanfadh sé, cuir becomes chuirfeadh sé. L, n, r and sc, sp, st, sm take no séimhiú (lasfadh, rithfeadh).
steps: Find the root: glan.
Add séimhiú: ghlan.
The last vowel is broad (a), so add -fadh: ghlanfadh.
Put the verb first: Ghlanfadh sé an scáileán.

example.prompt: (Glan) sé an scáileán.
example.answer: Ghlanfadh sé an scáileán.

more.answer: Chuirfeadh sé an mála sa charr.

lessons.hint: Séimhiú, then -fadh (broad) or -feadh (slender).

lessons.title: D' roimh ghuta agus roimh f
lessons.en: D' before a vowel and before f
lessons.rule: If the verb begins with a vowel, put d' in front of it (ól becomes d'ólfadh sé); if it begins with f, add séimhiú and put d' in front (fan becomes d'fhanfadh sé).
steps: Find the root: ól.
It begins with a vowel, so put d' in front: d'ól.
Add -fadh (broad): d'ólfadh.
Put the verb first: D'ólfadh sé an t-uisce.

example.prompt: (Ól) sé an t-uisce.
example.answer: D'ólfadh sé an t-uisce.

more.answer: D'fhágfadh sé an fón sa mhála.

lessons.hint: Vowel: d'. F: d'fh.

lessons.title: Freagra: -fainn / -finn
lessons.rule: When the question asks tú (-fá / -feá), answer with mé: add -fainn to a broad root or -finn to a slender root, with séimhiú or d' for yes and Ní for no (Chaithfinn nó ní chaithfinn).
steps: Find the root in the question: an gcaithfeá has the root caith.
Add séimhiú and -finn (slender) for yes: Chaithfinn.
Put ní before it for no: ní chaithfinn.
Fill both gaps: Chaithfinn nó ní chaithfinn.

lessons.title: Dá: an modh coinníollach sa dá leath
lessons.en: Dá: the conditional in both halves
lessons.rule: After dá (if), both halves of the sentence use the conditional: Dá mbeadh tart orm, d'ólfainn tae. Work out the person from the dá half (orm, mo, mbeinn all point to mé).
steps: Read the dá half to find the person: orm, so mé.
Put the verb in the conditional with the mé ending: cuir becomes chuirfinn.
Write the whole sentence: Dá mbeadh an lá fliuch, chuirfinn cóta fearthainne orm.

lessons.title: An saorbhriathar: -faí
lessons.rule: When no one is named (it would be done), add -faí to a broad root, with séimhiú or d' as usual: mol becomes mholfaí, ól becomes d'ólfaí.
steps: Find the root: mol.
Add séimhiú: mhol.
The root is broad, so add -faí: mholfaí.
Put the verb first: Mholfaí na gasúir dá mbeidís ciúin.

lessons.hint: Broad root + -faí.

lessons.title: An saorbhriathar: -fí
lessons.rule: With a slender root, add -fí instead, with séimhiú or d' as usual: cuir becomes chuirfí, éist becomes d'éistfí.
steps: Find the root: caith.
Add séimhiú: chaith.
The root is slender, so add -fí: chaithfí.
Put the verb first: Chaithfí an éide scoile.

r1-gnathchaite.title: An chéad réimniú: an aimsir ghnáthchaite

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, an chéad réimniú, briathra leathana
rules.text: To form the habitual past of a broad first-conjugation verb, lenite the initial consonant and add the endings: -ainn (mé), -tá (tú), -adh sé/sí, -adh muid, -adh sibh, -aidís (siad). The order form Dún gives Dhúnainn, Dhúntá, Dhúnadh sé, Dhúnadh muid, Dhúnadh sibh, Dhúnaidís. (The standard has the synthetic Dhúnaimis for the first person plural.)

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, an chéad réimniú, briathra caola
rules.text: A slender first-conjugation verb takes the same pattern with slender spellings of the endings: -inn, -teá, -eadh sé/sí, -eadh muid, -eadh sibh, -idís. Cuir gives Chuirinn, Chuirteá, Chuireadh sé, Chuireadh muid, Chuireadh sibh, Chuiridís. (The standard has Chuirimis.)

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, an dara pearsa uatha
rules.text: The pupil is expected to use it rather than dhúnadh tú.

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, an dara pearsa iolra
rules.text: With sibh there is no synthetic ending: the third-person form is used with the pronoun, Dhúnadh sibh, Chuireadh sibh, D'óladh sibh. When the question is put with sibh, the answer is given in the first person plural with muid (An ndúnadh sibh? Dhúnadh muid). The standard answers Dhúnaimis.

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, briathra a thosaíonn ar ghuta
rules.text: A first-conjugation verb beginning with a vowel takes d' before it in the habitual past: Ól gives D'óladh sé, D'ólainn, D'óltá; Úsáid gives D'úsáideadh sé, D'úsáidinn. After Ní and An the d' is dropped and nothing is prefixed: Ní ólainn, An óltá?

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, briathra a thosaíonn ar f
rules.text: A first-conjugation verb beginning with f is lenited and takes d' as well: Fág gives D'fhágadh sé, D'fhágainn, D'fhágtá. In the negative the d' is dropped but the lenition stays: Ní fhágadh sé, Ní fhágtaí. In the question the f is eclipsed: An bhfágtá? An bhfágaidís?

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, an fhoirm dhiúltach
rules.text: The negative is formed with Ní, which lenites the verb: Ní dhúnainn, Ní chuireadh sé. With vowel and f verbs the d' disappears: Ní óladh muid, Ní úsáidtí, Ní fhágaidís. (The standard has Ní ólaimis for the first person plural.)

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, an fhoirm cheisteach
rules.text: The question is formed with An, which eclipses the verb: An ndúntá? An gcuireadh sé? An bhfágadh sibh? A vowel-initial verb takes no change after An: An óladh sí? An úsáidtí?

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, an saorbhriathar
rules.text: Negative: Ní dhúntaí, Ní fhágtaí. Question: An ndúntaí? An bhfágtaí?

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite agus an modh coinníollach, comparáid
rules.text: (The standard sets Dhúnaimis beside Dhúnfaimis.)

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, an chéad phearsa iolra (nóta Ultach)
rules.text: In Ulster school usage the analytic form with muid is used instead: dhúnadh muid, chuireadh muid, d'óladh muid, d'fhágadh muid, and in the negative ní dhúnadh muid, ní óladh muid. The first person singular stays synthetic: dhúnainn, chuirinn.

lessons.title: Séimhiú agus -adh / -eadh
lessons.rule: To say what someone used to do, put séimhiú on the verb and add -adh to a broad root or -eadh to a slender root: cuir becomes chuireadh sé, glan becomes ghlanadh sé. Use this form with sé, sí, muid, sibh and a noun; l, n, r and sc, sp, st, sm take no séimhiú (lasadh, scuabadh).
steps: Find the root: cuir.
Add séimhiú: chuir.
The last vowel is slender (i), so add -eadh: chuireadh.
Put the verb first: Chuireadh sé an fón póca sa mhála.

example.prompt: (Cuir) sé an fón póca sa mhála.
example.answer: Chuireadh sé an fón póca sa mhála.

more.answer: Ghlanadh sé an scáileán.
Lasadh sé an solas.

r2-coinniollach.title: An dara réimniú: an modh coinníollach

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, an dara réimniú, briathra leathana (-aigh)
rules.text: For a second-conjugation verb ending in a broad -aigh (brostaigh, ceannaigh, críochnaigh), drop the -aigh and add -ódh for the third person (Bhrostódh sé, Cheannódh sé), and lenite the initial consonant.

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, an dara réimniú, briathra caola (-igh)
rules.text: For a second-conjugation verb ending in a slender -igh (bailigh, mínigh, deisigh, dúisigh), drop the -igh and add -eodh (Bhaileodh sé, Mhíneodh sé), again with lenition of the initial consonant.

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, na foirmeacha pearsanta (-óinn, -ófá, -óimis, -óidís, -ófaí)
rules.text: The personal endings in Ulster school usage are -óinn (mé), -ófá (tú), -ódh sé/sí, -ódh muid, -ódh sibh, -ódh siad and -ófaí (saorbhriathar); slender verbs take -eoinn, -eofá, -eodh, -eodh muid, -eodh sibh, -eodh siad, -eofaí. The first person singular stays synthetic (Cheannóinn, Bhaileoinn).

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, ceist agus diúltach (An + urú, Ní + séimhiú)
rules.text: A question takes An and eclipses the verb (An gceannófá? An mbaileodh sé?); the negative takes Ní and lenites (Ní cheannóinn, Ní bhaileodh sé). The positive answer is the lenited form on its own (Cheannóinn, Bhaileodh sé).

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, briathra a thosaíonn ar ghuta
rules.text: A second-conjugation verb beginning with a vowel takes d' in the positive (D'aeródh sé, D'ullmhódh sé, D'aimseodh sé). After An there is no change and no d' (An ullmhófá? An aimseodh sé?), and after Ní there is no d' either (Ní ullmhóinn, Ní aimseodh sé).

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, briathra a thosaíonn ar f
rules.text: A second-conjugation verb beginning with f takes d'fh in the positive (D'fhiosródh sé, D'fholmhódh sé), bhf after An (An bhfiosrófá?) and fh after Ní (Ní fhiosróinn).

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, an saorbhriathar (-ófaí, -eofaí)
rules.text: The autonomous form ends in -ófaí for broad verbs and -eofaí for slender verbs, with the same initial changes as the other persons: Cheannófaí, Bhaileofaí, D'ullmhófaí, D'aimseofaí, D'fhiosrófaí; An gceannófaí? Ní cheannófaí.

rules.point: an modh coinníollach, clásail choinníollacha (dá, mura)
rules.text: In Ulster school usage the plural forms inside those clauses are analytic too: dá mbeadh siad, dá gcuirfeadh siad (dá gcuirfidís), mura dtuigfeadh siad (mura dtuigfidís); dá mbeadh, dá mb'fhéidir leo, dá bhfeicfeadh sé, dá gcuirfinn and dá mbéarfadh sé are unchanged.

lessons.rule: For a verb ending in -aigh, put séimhiú on the first letter and change -aigh to -ódh: ceannaigh becomes cheannódh sé.

Add séimhiú: cheannaigh.
Change -aigh to -ódh: cheannódh.

r2-gnathchaite.title: An dara réimniú: an aimsir ghnáthchaite

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, an dara réimniú: briathra in -aigh
rules.text: To form the habitual past of a second-conjugation verb ending in -aigh, lenite the initial consonant and replace -aigh with -aíodh for sé/sí (Brostaigh becomes Bhrostaíodh sé, Ceannaigh becomes Cheannaíodh sé). The tense answers the question Cad é a dhéanadh sé? (what used he to do?).

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, an dara réimniú: briathra in -igh
rules.text: For a second-conjugation verb ending in -igh (slender), lenite and replace -igh with -íodh: Bailigh becomes Bhailíodh sé, Mínigh becomes Mhíníodh sé, Dúisigh becomes Dhúisíodh sé.

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, na foircinn phearsanta
rules.text: The endings are -aínn/-ínn (mé), -aíteá/-íteá (tú), -aíodh/-íodh sé or sí, -aíodh/-íodh muid, -aíodh/-íodh sibh, -aídís/-ídís (siad), with the saorbhriathar in -aítí/-ítí: Cheannaínn, Cheannaíteá, Cheannaíodh sé, Cheannaíodh muid, Cheannaíodh sibh, Cheannaídís, Cheannaítí. The first person plural is analytic in Ulster (cheannaíodh muid, not cheannaímis); the first person singular stays synthetic (cheannaínn). The standard form cheannaímis will be met in printed books and in the exam and should be recognised.

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, briathra a thosaíonn ar f
rules.text: A second-conjugation verb beginning with f takes d' as well as lenition in the positive: D'fhiosraíodh sé, D'fholmhaíodh sé. In the negative the d' is dropped and only the lenition remains: Ní fhiosraíodh sé. The question form eclipses: An bhfiosraíodh sé?

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, briathra a thosaíonn ar ghuta
rules.text: A verb beginning with a vowel takes d' in the positive (D'athraíodh sé, D'oibrídís, D'ullmhaínn) but not after Ní or An: Ní ullmhaínn, Ní aimsínn, An ullmhaíteá?, An aimsíteá?

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, an fhoirm dhiúltach
rules.text: The negative is formed with Ní followed by lenition and no d': Ní cheannaínn, Ní bhailínn, Ní fhiosraínn, Ní ullmhaínn.

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, an fhoirm cheisteach
rules.text: The question is formed with An followed by eclipsis: An gceannaíteá?, An mbailíteá?, An bhfiosraíteá?; a vowel-initial verb takes no change after An: An ullmhaíteá?

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite, an saorbhriathar
rules.text: The saorbhriathar (autonomous form) of the habitual past ends in -aítí or -ítí, with lenition on a consonant and d' before a vowel or f: Cheannaítí, Bhailítí, D'ullmhaítí, D'aimsítí, D'fhiosraítí, D'fhoilsítí leabhair sa chló Ghaelach.

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite agus an modh coinníollach: comparáid
rules.text: In both tenses the first person plural is analytic with muid in Ulster.

nr-coinniollach.title: Na briathra neamhrialta: an modh coinníollach

rules.point: na briathra neamhrialta, an modh coinníollach: na foirmeacha
rules.text: The section opens with a story in which each of these is used once in bold.

rules.point: an modh coinníollach: an fhoirm dhearfach (séimhiú agus d')
rules.text: Rachadh, déarfadh and gheobhadh are already in their fixed conditional shape and take no further change.

rules.point: an modh coinníollach: na deirí pearsanta
rules.text: The personal endings are the same as for regular verbs: -(f)ainn (mé), -(f)á (tú), -(f)adh sé/sí, -(f)adh muid, -(f)adh sibh, -(f)aidís (siad), plus the saorbhriathar in -(f)aí or -(f)í. The first person singular stays synthetic: bheinn, rachainn, d'íosfainn.

rules.point: an modh coinníollach: an fhoirm dhiúltach (Ní)
rules.text: The negative is formed with Ní and lenition: Ní bhéarfadh, Ní chloisfeadh, Ní thiocfadh, Ní thabharfadh, Ní dhéanfadh, Ní fheicfeadh, Ní bheadh. Ní íosfadh and Ní déarfadh (and Ní rachadh) have no lenition, and faigh is the odd one out with eclipsis: Ní bhfaigheadh, Ní bhfaighinn, Ní bhfaighfí.

rules.point: an modh coinníollach: an fhoirm cheisteach (An)
rules.text: The question is formed with An and eclipsis: An mbéarfadh, An gcloisfeadh, An dtiocfadh, An íosfadh, An dtabharfadh, An ndéanfadh, An bhfeicfeadh, An ndéarfadh, An rachadh, An bhfaigheadh, An mbeadh. The answer repeats the verb with its pronoun, positive or negative: Rachadh sé. Ní rachadh sé.

rules.point: dá agus an modh coinníollach
rules.text: The if-clause uses dá followed by eclipsis and the conditional: dá mbeadh, dá gcuirfinn, dá bhfaigheadh, dá mbeadh muid, dá mbeidís, dá rachaidís. Both halves of a conditional sentence are in the conditional mood: Dá mbeadh deich míle punt ag Pól, thabharfadh sé cuid de dá thuismitheoirí.

rules.point: an saorbhriathar sa mhodh coinníollach
rules.text: The autonomous form ends in -faí or -fí and has no subject: Thabharfaí cuidiú dóibh dá mbeidís i gcruachás. Positive forms keep the lenition and d' (D'íosfaí, D'fheicfí, Bhéarfaí, Chloisfí, Thiocfaí, Dhéanfaí, Bheifí); Rachfaí, Déarfaí and Gheofaí are fixed. Negative: Ní bhéarfaí, Ní chloisfí, Ní íosfaí, Ní bhfaighfí, Ní bheifí. Question: An mbéarfaí?, An gcloisfí?, An bhfaighfí?, An mbeifí?

rules.point: na focail cheiste sa mhodh coinníollach (Uladh)
rules.text: becomes Cad é a dhéanfá?; Cathain a déarfadh duine? becomes Cá huair a déarfadh duine?; Cá rachfá? and Cá bhfaighfeá? become Cá háit a rachfá? and Cá háit a bhfaighfeá? (the a before the verb keeps the eclipsis). Cén teanga a chloisfeá? is the same in Ulster.

rules.point: nóta don eagarthóir: botúin chló sa leabhar
rules.text: Page 96: 'Tabharfá' (tabhair) should be Thabharfá; 'Ní rachfainn' (téigh) should be Ní rachainn; 'Bheifea' (bí) should be Bheifeá. Page 95: the Beir table is headed 'Béir' and prints 'Bhearfainn' without the fada (Bhéarfainn); the Clois table prints 'Chloisfidí' for Chloisfidís.

rules.point: nóta don eagarthóir: foirmeacha Uladh sa mhodh coinníollach
rules.text: In Ulster the positive independent forms are also tchífeadh sé, tchífinn, tchífí. and Ní fheicfeadh sé; Tchífinn, but Ní fheicfinn and An bhfeicfinn). Two other Ulster vocabulary choices made below and worth a glance: de dhíth (for ag teastáil) and cuidiú (for cabhrú, cúnamh); i ndiaidh tamaill (for tar éis tamaill); achan lá, achan duine (for gach lá, gach éinne); gan airgead ar bith (for gan aon airgead).

nr-gnathchaite.title: Na briathra neamhrialta: an aimsir ghnáthchaite

rules.point: na briathra neamhrialta, an aimsir ghnáthchaite: an fhoirm dhearfach
rules.text: The initial consonant is lenited and d' is prefixed to a vowel or to fh, exactly as with regular verbs. Ulster usage is the same; the school keeps d'fheiceadh rather than the more local tchíodh.

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite: na foirceanna pearsanta
rules.text: The first person singular stays synthetic: théinn, bhínn, d'fhaighinn.

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite: an fhoirm dhiúltach agus cheisteach
rules.text: The negative is formed with ní plus lenition (ní théadh sé, ní bhíodh sé) and the question with an plus eclipsis (an dtéadh sé?, an mbíodh sé?). Verbs beginning with a vowel take nothing after ní and nothing after an (ní itheadh sé, an itheadh sé?); after ní the d' is dropped and an fh- verb shows the lenited form (ní fheiceadh sé, ní fhaigheadh sé). Abair does not lenite after ní: ní deireadh sé. Note that faigh takes ní fhaigheadh in the habitual past; the eclipsed ní bhfaigheadh belongs to the conditional only.

rules.point: an aimsir ghnáthchaite: an saorbhriathar
rules.text: The saorbhriathar of the habitual past ends in -tí or -taí (chloistí, d'ití, d'fheictí, thugtaí, d'fhaightí, deirtí, bhítí, thagtaí, dhéantaí, théití, bheirtí), with the same initial lenition or d' as the personal forms. Negative: ní chloistí; question: an gcloistí? Ulster usage is the same.

rules.point: nóta Uladh: foirmeacha táite an iolra
rules.text: The first person singular synthetic forms (théinn, bhínn, d'fhaighinn) are kept.

lessons.title: Séimhiú agus -adh
lessons.rule: Most irregular verbs work like regular ones in this tense: put séimhiú on the stem and add -adh or -eadh (bí gives bhíodh, téigh gives théadh, tar gives thagadh, tabhair gives thugadh, déan gives dhéanadh, cluin gives chluineadh, beir gives bheireadh).
steps: Find the stem of the verb: téigh uses té.
Add séimhiú: thé.
Add -adh: théadh.
Put the verb first: Théadh sé chuig traenáil peile achan oíche.

rules.point: na réamhfhocail shimplí, an liosta
rules.text: The simple prepositions covered are ar, ag, as, roimh, thar, idir, chuig, gan, faoi, le, do, de, ó, trí and i.

rules.point: réamhfhocal agus an t-alt 'an'
rules.text: Some prepositions fuse with the singular article an: faoi + an gives faoin, le + an gives leis an, do + an gives don, de + an gives den, ó + an gives ón, trí + an gives tríd an, i + an gives sa. Before a vowel or fh, sa becomes san (san fhómhar, san oíche, san áit). The rest simply stand before it: ar an, ag an, as an, roimh an, thar an, idir an, chuig an, gan an.

rules.point: réamhfhocal agus an t-alt 'na'
rules.text: Before the plural article na the prepositions are ar na, ag na, as na, roimh na, thar na, idir na, chuig na, gan na, faoi na, leis na, do na, de na, ó na, tríd na, and i + na gives sna.

rules.point: séimhiú i ndiaidh réamhfhocail shimplí
rules.text: Lenition follows these simple prepositions when there is no article: ar, roimh, thar, faoi, do, de, gan, idir, ó, trí (trí bhalla, trí Ghaeilge). The less common preposition um also lenites (um Cháisc).

rules.point: urú i ndiaidh 'i'
rules.text: Eclipsis follows the preposition i (i bpáirc, i gcruachás), but before a vowel it becomes in with no change to the noun (in Éirinn).

rules.point: ar an, ar na: consain
rules.text: In Ulster, after ar an (and after every simple preposition plus the singular article) initial b, c, f, g, m and p are lenited, not eclipsed: ar an bhord, ar an chailín, ar an fhuinneog, ar an gheata, ar an pháirc. After ar na no change is made to any consonant, whether b, c, f, g, p or d, n, t, l, s (ar na buachaillí, ar na cailíní, ar na fuinneoga, ar na geataí, ar na páirceanna).

rules.point: ar an, ar na: gutaí
rules.text: After ar an a vowel-initial noun is unchanged (ar an asal, ar an éan, ar an iascaire, ar an oráiste, ar an úll). After ar na, h is prefixed to a vowel (ar na hasail, ar na héin, ar na hiascairí, ar na horáistí, ar na húlla).

rules.point: ar an: d, n, t, l, s gan athrú
rules.text: Nouns beginning with d, n, t, l or s take no change after ar an: ar an trá, ar an líne, ar an nuachtán, ar an droichead, ar an sagart. Exception: a feminine noun beginning with s followed by a vowel or l, n, r takes t before the s (ar an tsráid, ar an tsúil).

rules.point: 'ar' le mothúcháin agus staid
rules.text: The preposition ar is used with words for feelings and states such as áthas, brón, fearg, eagla, imní, gliondar, díomá, ionadh, faitíos, náire, lúcháir, áiféala, uaigneas, scanradh, tuirse, ocras, amhras, bród, leisce, tart and éad: Tá ocras orthu, Tá tuirse air, Tá lúcháir uirthi. In Ulster lúcháir is the everyday word for áthas, and both are understood.

rules.point: 'ar' gan séimhiú i bhfrásaí seasta
rules.text: Lenition is not applied after ar in set phrases such as ar saoire, ar meisce, ar crochadh, ar buile, ar cairde, ar ceal, ar crith, ar díol, ar fáil, ar fónamh, ar mire, ar seachrán, ar siúl, ar iarraidh, ar iasacht, ar oscailt, ar lorg.

rules.point: do, don: uatha
rules.text: Lenition follows do (do Phól, do Mháire) and don (don bhuachaill, don chailín, don fhile, don ghirseach, don pháiste), except that nouns beginning with d, n, t, l, s or r are unchanged after don (don sagart, don tiománaí), and a vowel-initial noun takes no change after don (don aisteoir, don oibrí). Exception: a feminine noun beginning with s followed by a vowel or l, n, r takes t before the s (don tsráid, don tseanbhean).

rules.point: do na: iolra
rules.text: After do na a consonant-initial noun is unchanged (do na páistí, do na gardaí, do na múinteoirí) and h is prefixed to a vowel (do na huain, do na héin, do na haisteoirí, do na hainmhithe).

rules.point: ag, ag an, ag na
rules.text: No change follows ag on its own (ag Úna, ag Siobhán). In Ulster, after ag an, initial b, c, f, g, m and p are lenited (ag an bhuachaill, ag an chailín, ag an fháinleog, ag an gheata, ag an phíolóta) and a vowel is unchanged (ag an aisteoir, ag an éan, ag an iascaire, ag an othar, ag an uan). After ag na a consonant is unchanged (ag na buachaillí, ag na cailíní, ag na fáinleoga, ag na geataí, ag na píolótaí) and h is prefixed to a vowel (ag na hainmhithe, ag na héin, ag na hiascairí, ag na hothair, ag na huain).

rules.point: ag an: d, n, t, l, s gan athrú
rules.text: Nouns beginning with d, t, l, s or n take no change after ag an: ag an doras, ag an tarracóir, ag an lampa, ag an siopa, ag an nead. Exception: a feminine noun beginning with s followed by a vowel or l, n, r takes t before the s (ag an tsráid, ag an tseanbhean).

rules.point: an forainm réamhfhoclach
rules.text: Each simple preposition combines with the personal pronouns to make a prepositional pronoun (ar + mé gives orm, do + mé gives dom, ag + mé gives agam, and so on); idir has plural forms only (eadrainn, eadraibh, eatarthu).
